featured_reviews.name: Bhavika Mehta-Worah
featured_reviews.review_text:
This has been one of the most disappointing medical experiences I’ve had. We visited this cardiologist for a second opinion, bringing along an angiography CD to assess the percentage of blockage and determine whether angioplasty was necessary or if medication could suffice.

Unfortunately, the doctor was unable to confidently read the CD. Initially, he said he wasn’t sure if there was any blockage at all (raising serious doubts about his expertise as a cardiologist). Then, within just 15 minutes, his diagnosis fluctuated from no blockage, to 30%, to 70%, and finally 70–80%. This inconsistency was alarming and did not inspire confidence.

He began the consultation by noting blood pressure, weight, and other basic vitals. While reviewing the case history and previously prescribed medications, he recommended discontinuing *Cortel-CH* (prescribed by another doctor), claiming it could cause headaches and flush sodium from the body. However, he soon became confused, tore up the initial prescription, and scribbled a new one—this time only listing *Ecosprin Gold-40*, with no other notes or patient details.
